ONLINE METHODS

Generation of C24 mice. C24 mice with transgenic expression of a TCR specific for the I-A^b–ESAT6(1–20) antigen of M. tuberculosis were generated on the C57BL/6 (B6) background as previously described for the C7 mice^22. The transgene encoding the C24 TCR is driven by the human CD2 promoter and expresses the TCRα chain variable region 13.1 and joining region 32 (Vα11-Jα32) and TCRβ chain variable region 4, diversity region 2.1 and joining region 2.1 (Vβ4-Dβ2.1-Jβ2.1).

Mouse models. B6. PL-Thy1^a/CyJ (B6.PL), B6.129S7-Rag1^tm1Mom/J (Rag1^−/−) and B6.129S2-H2d1^b1-Ea/J (MHCII^−/−) mice were purchased from the Jackson Laboratory. All animal procedures were performed in agreement with approved protocols by the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. C7 and C24 mice were bred to B6.PL and Rag1^−/− mice (which lack mature B cells and T cells) to generate Rag1^−/− C7.PL and Rag1^−/− C24.PL mice, which were used as CD4^+ T cell donors in all experiments. C7 and C24 mice were maintained in the heterozygous state for the TCR-encoding transgenes. All animals were used between 6 and 12 weeks of age, were maintained under specific pathogen-free conditions in individually ventilated cages, were kept on a 12 h light-dark cycle and had access to food and water ad libitum. The sizes of the experimental groups were determined by the investigators without the use of statistical methods. All age- and sex-matched mice of a given strain were considered genetically identical and were randomly assigned to treatment groups, without the knowledge of the investigator to mouse identity. Both male and female mice were used throughout the study; however, T cell donors and recipients were always sex matched. In case T cell recipients showed clear signs of graft rejection (>10-fold lower T cell frequency compared to any other mouse in the same experimental group), these samples were excluded from further analysis.

MHC class II tetramer staining and cell sorting. MHC class II tetramer staining was performed as described^22. In brief, splenocytes were prepared from C7 and C24 TCR transgenic mice and stained with phycoerythrin (PE)-labeled I-A^b–ESAT6(1–20) tetramers (NIH Tetramer Core Facility) for 1 h at 37 °C. Cells were washed and stained with anti-PE microbeads (Miltenyi Biotec) and enriched using LS columns (both Miltenyi Biotec). To prepare antigen-presenting cells, B6 splenocytes were depleted of endogenous T cells using CD90.2 MicroBeads and LS columns, after which remaining splenocytes were irradiated with 25 Gy. 4 × 10^6 CD4^+ T cells were co-cultured with 1.2 × 10^6 irradiated antigen-presenting cells in RPMI medium containing 5 μg ml^−1 ESAT6(1–20) peptide, 10 ng ml^−1 recombinant mouse IL-12 (R&D Systems) and 5 μg ml^−1 neutralizing antibody to mouse IL-4 (11B11 hybridoma). Cells were cultured in 6-well plates at 37 °C and 5% CO_2. On days 2 and 3 of culture, cells were split in half and 12.5 ng ml^−1 recombinant mouse IL-2 (R&D Systems) was added. On day 4 of culture, C7 and C24 T_H1 cells were harvested, washed in PBS and transferred intravenously into sex-matched B6 recipients.

For in vitro cell proliferation assays, purified C7 and C24 T cells were resuspended in PBS containing 0.1% BSA and labeled with 5 μM CFSE (Invitrogen) for 10 min at 37 °C. After washing in RPMI medium, cells were activated using antigen-presenting cells as described above. The percentage divided cells was calculated using the Proliferation tool of FlowJo software.

For adoptive transfer of naive C7 and C24 T cells, CD4^+ T cells were purified from pooled spleen and lymph nodes of donor mice using the CD4^+ T cell Isolation Kit (Miltenyi Biotec) and LS columns to generate untouched CD4^+ T cells. Following washing in PBS, 1 × 10^6 CD4^+ T cells were transferred intravenously into sex-matched B6 recipients.

M. tuberculosis infection and T cell analysis. M. tuberculosis Erdman was grown in Middlebrook 7H9 broth (BD Biosciences) containing 10% OADC (BD Biosciences) and 0.05% Tween 80 (Fisher Scientific) to mid-log phase (OD_600 of ~0.2). Cultures were washed in PBS containing 0.05% Tween 80 (Fisher Scientific) and resuspended in PBS containing water. B6 mice were infected with aerosolized bacteria using an inhalation exposure system (Glas-Col), which was calibrated to deliver ~200 colony-forming units (CFU) per mouse. To assess bacterial burden, lungs were homogenized in 1 ml PBS containing 5 mM EDTA (US Biological), followed by serial dilution and plating on Middlebrook 7H11 agar (BD Biosciences) and incubation for 21 d at 37 °C and 5% CO_2, after which the number of colonies was determined.

For intracellular cytokine staining, lung cells were isolated as described above and resuspended in RPMI medium containing 1-glutamine, 25 mM HEPES, 10% FBS and 50 μM 2-mercaptoethanol (Invitrogen) for 1 h at 37 °C. For tetramer dissociation, cells were incubated as above but with the addition of 0.1% NaN_3. After washing to remove tetramer internalization, and dissociation was followed after washing free tetramer away. For intracellular cytokine staining, cells stained with PE tetramer were incubated with anti-PE MicroBeads and LS columns (both Miltenyi Biotec). For restimulation, cells were incubated in RPMI medium containing GolgiStop (BD Biosciences) and 5 μg ml^−1 I-A^b–ESAT6(1–20) peptide or 50 ng ml^−1 phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA; Calbiochem) and 1 μg ml^−1 ionomycin (Sigma-Aldrich) for 5 h at 37 °C. For surface staining, cells were incubated in PBS containing 0.5% bovine serum albumin (BSA; Sigma-Aldrich) and 0.1% NaN_3 for 15 min at 4 °C. For intracellular staining, cells were fixed and permeabilized after cell surface staining with Cytofix/Cytoperm solution (BD Biosciences) for 15 min at 4 °C, followed by blocking in Perm/Wash solution (BD Biosciences) for 15 min at 4 °C and staining for intracellular proteins in Perm/Wash solution for 15 min at 4 °C. For nuclear staining, cells were stained using a Foxp3 Staining Buffer set (eBioscience). Antibodies to the following proteins were used (clone numbers and dilutions in parentheses): Supplementary Table 1): CD3ε (145-2C11; 1:100), CD4 (RM4-5; 1:100), CD8 (53-7.3; 1:100), CD8α (53-6.7; 1:50), CD25 (PC61; 1:100), CD27 (LG.3A10; 1:100), CD28 (37.51; 1:50), CD44 (IM7; 1:100), CD45 (30-F11; 1:200), CD62L (MEL-14; 1:100), CD69 (H1.2F3; 1:50), CD90.1 (OX-7; 1:100), CD122 (TM-β1; 1:50), CTLA-4 (UC10-4F10-11; 1:50), IFN-γ (XMG1.2; 1:200), PD-1 (J43; 1:50), TCRβ (H57-597; 1:100), hamster IgG1 isotype control (A19-3; 1:50) and rat IgG2a isotype control (RTK2758; 1:100) (all BD Biosciences); CD127 (A7R34; 1:50) and Foxp3 (FJK-16s; 1:100) (both eBioscience); and TCR (H146-968; 1:100) (Thermo Scientific). Dead cells were excluded using 7-AAD Viability Staining Solution (eBioscience). Cells were measured on an LSRII flow cytometer (BD Biosciences) and data were analyzed using FlowJo software (TreeStar).

In vitro T_H1 differentiation and adoptive cell transfer. For in vitro T_H1 differentiation of C7 and C24 T cells, CD4^+ T cells from pooled spleen and lymph nodes of donor mice were purified using CD4 (L3T4) MicroBeads and LS columns (both Miltenyi Biotec). To prepare antigen-presenting cells, B6 splenocytes were depleted of endogenous T cells using CD90.2 MicroBeads and LS columns, after which remaining splenocytes were irradiated with 25 Gy. 4 × 10^6 CD4^+ T cells were co-cultured with 1.2 × 10^6 irradiated antigen-presenting cells in RPMI medium containing 5 μg ml^−1 ESAT6(1–20) peptide, 10 ng ml^−1 recombinant mouse IL-12 (R&D Systems) and 5 μg ml^−1 neutralizing antibody to mouse IL-4 (11B11 hybridoma). For in vitro cell proliferation assays, purified C7 and C24 T cells were resuspended in PBS containing 0.1% BSA and labeled with 5 μM CFSE (Invitrogen) for 10 min at 37 °C. Cultures were washed in PBS containing 0.05% Tween 80 (Fisher Scientific) and resuspended in PBS containing water. Immunoblot analysis. Naive C7 and C24 T cells were purified from spleens of donor mice using CD4 MicroBeads and LS columns. 1 × 10^6 cells were lysed in 100 μl RIPA buffer (Sigma-Aldrich) containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors (Thermo Scientific). 15 μl of lysates was mixed with 2× loading buffer, separated with 10% SDS-PAGE and transferred to PVDF membrane. Membranes were incubated with the primary antibodies rabbit antibody to TCRβ phosphorylated at Tyr142 (SAB4200343) and rabbit anti–β-actin (SAB5500001) (both Sigma-Aldrich) overnight at 4 °C, with a dilution factor of 1:1,000 in blocking buffer (PBS with 5% skim milk and 0.1% Tween 20). Following incubation with horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-linked anti-rabbit secondary antibody (7074; Cell Signaling; diluted 1:5,000 in blocking buffer), detection was performed using ECL reagent (GE Healthcare).
